_note: Demo cases shown on the Y-finder welcome screen. People are fictional; questions, places, data and Yale access routes are real. scripts/record_demos.py runs each script against the live agent and saves the event stream to static/demos/<id>.json so the app can replay it quickly and reliably, then continue live.

cases.title: Where do mosquitoes breed?
cases.who: Maya Chen (fictional), MPH student at the Yale School of Public Health, joining a New Haven larval-control pilot. First GIS project.
shows: Influence graph from a plain question
10 m satellite flagged too coarse for small pools
Yale aerial imagery and YCGS drone support
Recent aerial photo loaded on the map

steps.message: Which standing water sites in New Haven are most likely to breed Culex mosquitoes this summer, to guide larval control?

steps.note: Step 1 and 2 of tri-projection: the influence graph puts the outcome in the center and core factors on the inner ring. Below it, the scope: defaults are tagged so Maya can correct them.
Step 3: every dataset is checked against the scope by rules, not by the AI. Satellite imagery at 10 m cannot see small pools, so it is labeled a poor fit.

steps.message: Focus on the Fair Haven neighborhood for June to August 2026, and show me the most recent aerial imagery there.

steps.note: Recent aerial imagery for Fair Haven loads from Microsoft Planetary Computer, inside the new study area.

cases.title: Wildfire smoke and asthma
cases.who: Dr. Lena Ortiz (fictional), environmental health faculty. Her asthma team needs daily PM2.5 for every Connecticut census tract during the June 2023 Canadian wildfire smoke.
shows: Tract-level scope across a whole state
Monitors, satellite aerosol and smoke plumes combined

steps.message: Estimate daily PM2.5 exposure by census tract in Connecticut during the June 2023 wildfire smoke, for an asthma study.

steps.note: Monitors alone are too sparse for tracts, so Y-finder pairs EPA monitors with satellite aerosol and NOAA smoke plumes, and suggests how to validate the result.

steps.message: How do I download the EPA monitor data for Connecticut?

steps.title: EPA Air Quality System (AirData)
steps.note: Each source can carry an access handbook written like an Agent Skill: access route, endpoint, a Python example and pitfalls. Coding agents can use it too.

cases.title: Zoning reform and new housing
cases.who: Sam Rivera (fictional), economics PhD student. He attaches his one-page proposal instead of typing a question.
shows: Town-level scope for a policy study
Editing the scope re-checks every dataset

steps.message: Here is my proposal. Help me find data for it.

steps.note: Sam widens the window to start in 2016 to get five years before the reform. The fit labels update at once, with no new AI call.
The fit matrix compares every source on area, time, detail and access at a glance.

cases.title: New Haven's lost shoreline
cases.who: Ava Brooks (fictional), history PhD student writing about the harbor's industrial past.
shows: Live search of Yale Library map holdings
Hand-off to GeoLibre for full GIS

steps.message: Find historical maps of New Haven's waterfront from 1850 to 1950 so I can trace how the shoreline changed.

steps.note: Results come from a live search of Yale Library's GeoBlacklight portal, so they are real Yale holdings with record links.
Full GIS opens the same layers in GeoLibre, an open-source web GIS, with its menus collapsed until needed.

cases.title: Downtown recovery after COVID
cases.who: Priya Nair (fictional), MBA student at the School of Management, studying downtown retail in New Haven.
shows: Yale-licensed data (Dewey) with the access route

steps.message: How did foot traffic in downtown New Haven recover after COVID, from 2019 to 2023?

steps.note: Dewey Data is a Yale subscription; the card says how to get access with a Yale email, and what the data cannot show.
With her consent, Y-finder can search again on a schedule and post short updates to a private link.

cases.title: Malaria and land cover in western Kenya
cases.who: Kofi Mensah (fictional), global health MPH student planning field work around Kisumu.
shows: Global datasets for a study outside the US
US-only sources flagged as outside the area

steps.message: Map land cover change and malaria risk around villages near Kisumu, Kenya, from 2015 to 2025.

steps.note: The scope is set to western Kenya, so US-only datasets such as Census tables or NAIP would be labeled outside the study area.

steps.message: Show me a recent cloud-free satellite image of the study area.

steps.note: A recent Sentinel-2 scene over the study area, streamed from Planetary Computer.
